mainTopic: Guarantors for a כתובה, collecting debts from הקדש, and what a person who owes ערכין may keep
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רב הונא, whose father משה בר עצרי had guaranteed his כתובה. The גמרא says the father was a קַבְּלָן, a stronger guarantor, and gives two ways this works even though רב הונא was poor. It then quotes the full מחלוקת about which guarantors are bound, and rules that every guarantor is bound except an ordinary עָרֵב for a כתובה. Next comes a case about a wife who collects her כתובה from a buyer. רב פפא and the Sages of נהרדעא disagree about whether the husband must vow not to remarry her in that case. A new משנה teaches that a wife and a creditor cannot collect directly from הקדש. Instead, the property is redeemed, even for one דינר, and the גמרא explains why and how far this method reaches. A second משנה lists what the treasurer leaves for someone who owes ערכין: food, clothes, a bed, sandals, תפילין and work tools. The גמרא begins to give the פסוק behind this, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The father was a stronger kind of guarantor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier objection by saying משה בר עצרי was a קַבְּלָן, not an ordinary עָרֵב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (the father) was a קַבְּלָן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question just asked: how could the wife collect from the father if an ordinary guarantor of a כתובה is not bound? The answer is that the father was a קַבְּלָן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary עָרֵב only pays if the main person cannot pay. A קַבְּלָן takes full responsibility, so the lender, or here the wife, can go straight to him. Calling the father a קַבְּלָן means his obligation is strong enough that the wife can collect from him.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor who takes on full, direct responsibility for a debt; he can be approached first
An ordinary guarantor, who pays only if the main person cannot
The marriage contract that promises the wife money if the marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up עָרֵב and קַבְּלָן. Both are guarantors, but a קַבְּלָן is much more strongly bound. The whole section depends on that difference.

phrases.english: He was a kablan (unconditional guarantor).
phrases.notes: "He" means משה בר עצרי, רב הונא's father, who had guaranteed his son's כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection raised just before this section, that an ordinary עָרֵב for a כתובה is not bound.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the father was a קַבְּלָן, not an ordinary עָרֵב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father was an ordinary עָרֵב for the כתובה, so the wife could not collect from him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father was a קַבְּלָן, so he is bound and the wife can collect from him.

steps.title: This only works for one view of a קַבְּלָן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the answer works if a קַבְּלָן is bound even when the husband has no property, but not according to the view that he is bound only when the husband has property.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says a קַבְּלָן is bound even if the borrower has no property. But for the one who says that if the borrower has property the קַבְּלָן is bound, and if not he is not bound, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. רב הונא was poor, so according to one opinion even a קַבְּלָן would not be bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about whether a קַבְּלָן for a כתובה is bound when the husband owns nothing. The reasoning behind the stricter view is that a guarantor would not seriously commit himself for someone who has nothing to back the debt. Since רב הונא owned nothing, the answer "he was a קַבְּלָן" seems to work only for the first view.

keyTerms.meaning: "It works out fine" (according to one view); it sets up a challenge from the other view
The borrower, the main person who owes the debt
Becomes legally bound or obligated to pay
"What can be said?", a call for an answer to a difficulty

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says: a kablan,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ נְכָסִים לְלֹוֶה — מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד,
phrases.english: even though the borrower has no property, is bound,
phrases.notes: Here the "borrower" stands for the husband, who owes the כתובה.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says:
if he (the borrower) has property, he (the kablan) is bound,
if he does not have, he is not bound,
what can be said?
phrases.notes: רב הונא was poor, so according to this view his father should not be bound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 1 from the view of a disputing opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the father was a קַבְּלָן (step 1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that a קַבְּלָן is bound only when the husband has property, the father of the poor רב הונא would still not be bound.

steps.title: First answer: רב הונא once had property
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא did own property when his father became guarantor, but it was later ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: רב הונא had property, and it became blighted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: at the time of the guarantee רב הונא did own property, so even the stricter view would bind the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is the situation when the guarantee was made. Back then רב הונא had property, so the father's commitment was serious. The property was ruined only later, and that does not cancel the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you wish, say", which introduces one of several possible answers
It became blighted or ruined (as crops struck by a hot wind)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
Rav Huna had (property), and it became blighted,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַב הוּנָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ וְאִישְׁתְּדוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא never had property, so under the stricter view the father is not bound.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא had property at the time of the guarantee, so the father became bound even under the stricter view.

steps.title: Second answer: a father commits fully for his son
steps.stepSummary: A father seriously binds himself for his son even when the son has no property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: a father, regarding his son, fully binds himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer: even under the stricter view, a father is an exception and truly commits himself for his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stricter view rests on the idea that a guarantor does not seriously commit for someone with nothing. A father's love for his son changes that, so he means his commitment even if the son is poor. This answer does not need the facts of the first answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A father with regard to his son
He fully binds himself to the obligation

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
a father, with regard to his son,
truly binds himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a special exception for a father guaranteeing his son
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under the stricter view, no guarantor is bound for a husband who has no property.
steps.terutzMaskana: A father is an exception: he commits fully for his son even without property.

steps.title: The full disagreement about guarantors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full source: everyone agrees an ordinary עָרֵב for a כתובה is not bound and a קַבְּלָן for a loan is bound. For an עָרֵב for a loan and a קַבְּלָן for a כתובה there is a מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As was stated: an ordinary guarantor of a כתובה is not bound, according to everyone. A קַבְּלָן for a creditor is bound, according to everyone. A guarantor for a creditor and a קַבְּלָן for a כתובה are in dispute. One says: if the borrower has property he is bound, if not, he is not bound. Another says: even if he has none, he is bound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes in full the מחלוקת it was relying on in steps 2-4, laying out four kinds of guarantors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two extremes that everyone agrees on: the weakest case, an עָרֵב for a כתובה, is not bound, and the strongest case, a קַבְּלָן for a loan, is bound. The two middle cases are disputed, and the dispute depends on whether the main person owns property. The father's case, a קַבְּלָן for a כתובה, is one of the disputed middle cases, which is why the question in step 2 came up.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
A creditor, someone who lent money
They disagree

steps.whatToRemember: There are four cases. An עָרֵב for a כתובה: not bound, by everyone. A קַבְּלָן for a loan: bound, by everyone. An עָרֵב for a loan and a קַבְּלָן for a כתובה: disputed, depending on whether the main person has property.

phrases.english: As it was stated: a guarantor of a marriage contract,
according to everyone, is not bound;
a kablan for a creditor,
according to everyone, is bound;

phrases.aramaic: עָרֵב דְּבַעַל חוֹב וְקַבְּלָן דִּכְתוּבָּה — פְּלִיגִי.
phrases.english: a guarantor for a creditor and a kablan for a marriage contract: they disagree.
There is one who says:
if the borrower has property, he (the guarantor) is bound;
if he does not have, he is not bound;
and there is one who says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ — מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד.
phrases.english: even though he does not have, he is bound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full source of the dispute that step 2 referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עָרֵב for a כתובה is never bound and a קַבְּלָן for a loan is always bound. An עָרֵב for a loan and a קַבְּלָן for a כתובה are disputed, depending on whether the main person has property.

steps.title: The final ruling and its reason
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that every guarantor is bound even when the main person has no property, except an ordinary עָרֵב for a כתובה, who is never bound. He is doing a מצוה, and the wife lost nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה in all cases is that even if he has no property, the guarantor is bound, except for an עָרֵב of a כתובה, who is not bound even if the husband has property. Why? He is doing a מצוה, and she did not lose anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה for all four cases and explains why the ordinary עָרֵב for a כתובה is the one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows the view from step 5 that a guarantor is bound even when the main person has no property. The עָרֵב for a כתובה is different for two reasons. He signs only to help the marriage happen (a מצוה), without truly meaning to pay. Also, the wife gave nothing in return, unlike a lender who handed over money because of the guarantee.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical law is
Except for
What is the reason?
He is doing a מצוה, helping the marriage happen
He made her lose nothing; she gave up nothing because of the guarantee

steps.whatToRemember: In practice every guarantor, עָרֵב or קַבְּלָן, for a loan or a כתובה, is bound even if the main person has no property. The one exception is an ordinary עָרֵב for a כתובה, who is never bound, because he is doing a מצוה and the wife lost nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for guarantees. It also shows that a guarantee binds because the other side relied on it and gave something up; when nothing was given up, the guarantee is not taken as a real commitment.

phrases.english: And the halakha in all of them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ נָמֵי מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד,
phrases.english: even though he does not have (property), he is also bound,
except for a guarantor of a marriage contract,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לֵיהּ לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד.
phrases.english: who, even though he (the husband) has (property), is not bound.
What is the reason?
He is performing a מצוה,
phrases.notes: He only signed to help the marriage go through, not because he really meant to pay.

phrases.english: and he did not cause her any loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת quoted in step 5 and explains the one exception.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All guarantors are bound even when the main person has no property, except an ordinary עָרֵב for a כתובה, who is never bound, because he does a מצוה and caused the wife no loss.

steps.title: A new case: what if the wife collects from a buyer?
steps.stepSummary: A man sold his property and then divorced his wife. רב יוסף בריה דרבא asks רב פפא whether the rule for a ערב and for הקדש also covers a לוקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who sold his property and then divorced his wife. רב יוסף son of רבא sent a question to רב פפא: about a guarantor we have a teaching, and about consecrated property we have a teaching. What is the law with a buyer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case and asks a new question. Is a wife collecting from a buyer like the two cases we already know?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already have teachings that the husband must vow off his wife when she collects from a ערב or from הקדש. The husband here sold his land, so the wife can only collect from the לוקח who bought it. The question is whether the buyer gets the same protection.

keyTerms.meaning: A buyer, here the person who bought the husband's land
Property given to the בית המקדש (consecrated property)
What is the law? The standard way to ask a question

phrases.english: There was a certain man who sold his property,
and he was divorcing his wife.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording ('was divorcing her').

phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rava, sent it
before Rav Pappa:
A guarantor, we learned; consecrated property, we learned;
phrases.notes: He means we have a משנה for each of these cases saying the husband must vow not to benefit from her.

phrases.english: what about a buyer?

steps.triggerLanguage: עָרֵב תְּנַן, הֶקְדֵּשׁ תְּנַן, לוֹקֵחַ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the guarantor discussion to a new case, a buyer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the vow rule taught for a ערב and for הקדש also apply when the wife collects from a לוקח?

steps.title: רב פפא: the משנה does not list every case
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that a buyer is obviously the same. The תנא does not have to list every case like a peddler calling out his goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Should the Tanna keep listing case after case, like a peddler?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. A buyer is the same as the cases we learned, even though the משנה did not mention it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that a משנה gives examples, not a complete list. Since the same reasoning fits a buyer, the vow rule applies there too.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה
A peddler, who calls out every item he sells
Keep counting on and on

phrases.english: He said to him:
Should the Tanna, like a peddler,
keep listing and going on?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. He means: of course not, so a buyer is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A buyer is the same; the משנה just did not bother listing every case.

steps.title: The Sages of נהרדעא: only the cases taught
steps.stepSummary: The Sages of נהרדעא disagree with רב פפא. Only the cases actually taught need the vow, so a buyer does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages of נהרדעא say: What we learned, we learned. What we did not learn, we did not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion appears. It says the rule applies only to the cases the משנה names, not to a buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא read the משנה as giving examples. The Sages of נהרדעא read it as a careful, limited list. So in their view the husband does not have to vow when the wife collects from a לוקח.

keyTerms.meaning: What we learned is what we learned; do not stretch it
What was not taught is not included

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think נהרדעא is saying the משנה forgot the buyer. They hold the buyer was left out on purpose, because his case is different.

phrases.english: The Sages of Neharde'a say:
What we learned, we learned;
what we did not learn, we did not learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהַרְדָּעֵי אָמְרִי: דִּתְנַן תְּנַן, דְּלָא תְּנַן לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רב פפא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vow is required only for a ערב and for הקדש, not for a buyer.

steps.title: Why הקדש and the guarantor need protection
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא explains נהרדעא. הקדש is protected for the sake of the Temple's profit. The ערב is protected because he did a מצוה and got nothing from the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: What is the reasoning of the Sages of נהרדעא? It makes sense with consecrated property, because of the profit of הקדש. A guarantor too, because he did a מצוה, and she did not lose anything.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא starts explaining the view of נהרדעא. First he shows why the two cases the משנה lists do deserve the vow rule. This sets up the contrast with the buyer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הקדש, we care about the Temple's money. For the ערב, he helped her as a favor and got nothing back, so we protect him so people keep doing this מצוה. The next step shows that a buyer has no reason like these.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
It makes sense with... (sets up a contrast that is coming next)
The profit of הקדש, the Temple treasury

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
What is the reasoning of the Sages of Neharde'a?
Granted, with consecrated property,
it is because of the profit of the Temple treasury;
a guarantor also,
it is a מצוה that he did,
and she did not lose anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדש and the ערב each have a special reason for protection.

steps.title: The buyer brought the loss on himself
steps.stepSummary: Every buyer knows that married men owe a כתובה, so a buyer who bought anyway caused his own loss. That is why the vow rule does not protect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a buyer: after all, he knows that every single man has a כתובה on him. Why did he go and buy? He is the one who caused himself the loss!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא finishes the reasoning of נהרדעא by contrasting the buyer with the two protected cases. The buyer has no good claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike הקדש or the generous ערב, the buyer knew the land might be taken for a כתובה and bought it anyway. Since he took that risk himself, we do not stop the husband from remarrying his wife just to protect the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the contrasting case)
After all; since it is known
He caused a loss to himself

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: a buyer is the same as a ערב and הקדש. נהרדעא: a buyer is not protected, because he knowingly took the risk of a כתובה claim.

phrases.english: But a buyer,
after all, he surely knows

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל חַד וְחַד אִיכָּא עֲלֵיהּ כְּתוּבָּה,
phrases.english: that each and every man has a marriage contract on him;
why should he go and buy?
It is he who caused himself to lose!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun with בשלמא in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to נהרדעא, the husband need not vow when the wife collects from a buyer, since the buyer accepted the risk.

steps.title: New משנה: a wife and a creditor cannot collect from הקדש
steps.stepSummary: If someone makes his property הקדש while owing a כתובה and a debt, they cannot collect from הקדש. Whoever redeems the property takes it knowing he must pay them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone consecrates his property while he owes his wife's כתובה and a creditor, the wife cannot collect her כתובה from the consecrated property, and the creditor cannot collect his debt. Rather, whoever redeems the property redeems it on condition that he pays the wife her כתובה and the creditor his debt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It teaches that people owed money cannot take it straight from הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once property is הקדש, nobody can collect from the Temple directly. Instead, the property is redeemed from הקדש, and the redeemer takes it with the debts still attached to it. Then the wife and the creditor collect from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
One who gives his property to הקדש
A creditor, someone owed a loan
The one who redeems (buys back) the property from הקדש
On condition that

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who consecrates his property,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה עָלָיו כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה וּבַעַל חוֹב
phrases.english: and he owed a wife's marriage contract and a creditor,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הָאִשָּׁה יְכוֹלָה לִגְבּוֹת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: the woman cannot collect her marriage contract from the consecrated property,
nor the creditor his debt;
rather, the one who redeems, redeems
on condition to give the woman her marriage contract
and the creditor his debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו, וְהָיְתָה עָלָיו כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה וּבַעַל חוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Debts cannot be collected directly from הקדש. The redeemer takes the property with the debts still on it.

steps.title: When the debt is bigger than the property, add a dinar
steps.stepSummary: If the property is worth 90 מנה but the debt is 100 מנה, one more דינר is added. The property is redeemed with it, and the wife and the creditor are paid from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he consecrated property worth ninety מנה and his debt was a hundred מנה, he adds another דינר and redeems the property, on condition to give the woman her כתובה and the creditor his debt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a harder case. Here the debt is larger than the whole property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the debts eat up all the property's value, there is nothing left for הקדש. Still, the property must be redeemed with something, so a single דינר is added to redeem it. Then the debts are paid from it.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth 100 דינרים
A basic silver coin
He adds

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the redemption is needed even when הקדש gets almost nothing, so that the property can return to ordinary hands and pay its debts.

phrases.english: If he consecrated ninety maneh
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 דינרים, so this is property worth 9,000 against a debt of 10,000.

phrases.english: and his debt was one hundred maneh,
he adds another dinar,
and redeems these properties
on condition to give the woman her marriage contract
and the creditor his debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִקְדִּישׁ תִּשְׁעִים מָנֶה וְהָיָה חוֹבוֹ מֵאָה מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 12 to a case where the debt is larger than the property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the debt is larger than the property, a דינר is added so the property can be redeemed and the debts paid.

steps.title: Why does the property need to be redeemed at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says the property must be redeemed before the creditor gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need the משנה to say 'the one who redeems, redeems'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a question about the משנה's wording. It is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the end, the creditor and the wife get the property anyway. So why go through a formal redemption? Why not just hand the property straight to them?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question about why something had to be said or done
The one who redeems, redeems: the property must first be bought out of הקדש

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why do I need to say
'the one who redeems, redeems'?
phrases.notes: These words come from the first part of the משנה, in step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the redemption procedure described in steps 12-13, quoting the words of step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a formal redemption is required, instead of giving the property directly to the creditor and the wife

steps.title: So people will not think הקדש leaves without redemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the property is redeemed so that people will not say הקדש can become ordinary property without פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of רבי אבהו's teaching. רבי אבהו said: so that people should not say that הקדש goes out without redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with רבי אבהו's reason. The formal redemption protects people's respect for הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If creditors could just take הקדש property, people would get the wrong idea that holy property can become ordinary without being redeemed. The single דינר in the redemption makes the release official and visible.

keyTerms.meaning: So that people should not say: a rule made to stop a mistaken idea
Redemption: buying property out of הקדש so it becomes ordinary
Goes out: leaves holy status and becomes ordinary

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even when the money really goes to the creditor, the process must respect the holiness of הקדש.

phrases.english: Because of the teaching of רבי אבהו,
as רבי אבהו said:
so that people will not say
that הקדש goes out without redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Redemption is required so people will not think הקדש can become ordinary without פדיון

steps.title: Our משנה disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the extra-דינר method of our משנה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He allows it only when the debt matches the value of the הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It was taught in a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, if his debt matched his הקדש, he redeems it this way. If not, he does not redeem it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a ברייתא shows another view. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the extra-דינר method from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lets the property be redeemed for one דינר even when the property (90) is worth less than the debt (100). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says this works only when the debt equals the property's value. Otherwise the property must be redeemed at its real value.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow so-and-so's opinion
Matching, equal to
His debt

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Our משנה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
If his debt matched his הקדש property,
he redeems it this way,
and if not, he does not redeem it this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the method of step 13 is disputed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows the one-דינר redemption only when the debt equals the value of the הקדש

steps.title: How big a gap do the רבנן allow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far the רבנן's view stretches. How much smaller can the property be than the debt?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the limit of the רבנן's view. It is setting up רב ששת's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן of our משנה allow some gap between the debt and the property's value. But surely there is some limit. The גמרא wants to know where it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
Up to how much? A question asking for a limit

phrases.english: And the רבנן, up to how much?
phrases.notes: He is asking how much less than the debt the property can be worth and still use this method.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the limit of the opinion that disagrees with step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The largest gap between the debt and the property's value at which the רבנן still allow the one-דינר method

steps.title: Up to half
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the method works as long as the property is worth at least half of the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: up to half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer. The property must be worth at least half of the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the property is worth half the debt or more, the creditor can lend one דינר and redeem it. If it is worth less than half, it must be redeemed for its real value.

keyTerms.meaning: Half

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on redeeming הקדש for a debt with one extra דינר. The רבנן, the view of our משנה, allow it as long as the property is worth at least half the debt. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it only when the debt matches the property's value.

phrases.english: רב הונא בר יהודה said
that רב ששת said: up to half.
phrases.notes: The property must be worth at least half of what he owes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The method works as long as the property is worth at least half of the debt

steps.title: What a person who owes ערכין may keep
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the court takes property from people who owe ערכין, but leaves them food for 30 days, clothes for 12 months, a made bed, sandals and תפילין. These are for him only, not for his wife and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Even though they said that the court takes property from people who owe ערכין, they give him food for thirty days, clothing for twelve months, a made bed, his sandals and his תפילין. These are for him, but not for his wife and children.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the basic things the הקדש treasurer must leave for a man whose property is being taken to pay his ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court may take property to pay a ערך, but it does not leave the man with nothing. He keeps basic needs for himself. This protection covers only him personally, not his wife and children.

keyTerms.meaning: People who owe a ערך, a fixed valuation pledged to the Temple
Take property as a pledge to collect a debt
A bed made up with bedding
Clothing

steps.confusionAlert: The things he keeps are only for himself. The משנה clearly says they are not left for his wife and children.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Even though they said
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier משנה on 21a.

phrases.english: that those who owe valuations have their property taken,
phrases.notes: Some versions say אותו ('him') and others say אותן ('them'). The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: they give him food for thirty days,
and clothing for twelve months,
a made bed, his sandals, and his תפילין,
for him, but not for his wife and his children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ חַיָּיבֵי עֲרָכִין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic: what is left for someone whose property is taken
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When property is taken for ערכין, the man keeps 30 days of food, 12 months of clothing, a made bed, sandals and תפילין for himself, but not for his wife and children

steps.title: A craftsman keeps two tools of each kind
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. A craftsman may keep two tools of every type he uses. A carpenter, for example, keeps two adzes and two saws.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was a craftsman, the treasurer leaves him two tools of each type of his trade. A carpenter keeps two adzes and two saws.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing what the treasurer must leave for a person who owes ערכין. Now it adds work tools for a craftsman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה left him food, clothes, a bed, sandals and תפילין. Now it adds the tools he needs to earn a living. He gets two of each type, not just one, and the carpenter is given as an example.

keyTerms.meaning: A craftsman, a skilled worker
Tools of one's trade
Here: a carpenter or woodworker (not a deaf person)
Adzes, cutting tools used for shaping wood
Saws

steps.confusionAlert: Here חָרָשׁ means a carpenter, not the deaf person (חֵרֵשׁ) you may know from other סוגיות.

phrases.english: If he was a craftsman —
he gives him two tools of his craft
phrases.notes: "He" is the הקדש treasurer, who leaves these items with the person.

phrases.english: of each and every type,
a carpenter — they give him
two adzes and two saws.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of items left to the person who owes ערכין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A craftsman keeps two tools of each type of his trade.

steps.title: A farmer keeps his oxen and a donkey driver keeps his donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds to the list. A farmer keeps his pair of plowing animals, and a donkey driver keeps his donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: if he was a farmer, he keeps his pair of oxen. If he was a donkey driver, he keeps his donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר widens the idea of work tools. Animals a person works with also count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה spoke about hand tools. רבי אליעזר applies the same idea of keeping a livelihood to work animals. For a farmer that means the pair he plows with, and for a donkey driver his donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: A farmer who plows the land
His pair (of oxen) used for plowing
A donkey driver who carries loads for a living

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה אִיכָּר — נוֹתֵן לוֹ צִמְדּוֹ,
phrases.english: If he was a farmer — he gives him his pair (of oxen),
a donkey driver — he gives him his donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the work-tools rule by including work animals
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a farmer keeps his plowing pair and a donkey driver keeps his donkey.

steps.title: Many of one tool and few of another
steps.stepSummary: If he has many tools of one kind and few of another, the treasurer does not sell extra ones to buy more of the scarce kind. He leaves two of the plentiful kind and whatever he has of the scarce kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had many of one kind of tool and few of another, he cannot say: sell some of the many and buy me more of the few. Rather, he keeps two of the many, and all he has of the few.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a person whose tools are uneven, for example three adzes and one saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that he keeps what he actually owns, up to two of each type. The extras of the plentiful type go to הקדש. They are not exchanged to make up the missing ones of the scarce type, so he ends up with less than two of that type.

keyTerms.meaning: Plentiful, the type he has many of
Scarce, the type he has few of

steps.whatToRemember: The treasurer leaves only what the person already owns, up to two per type. He does not buy him missing tools.

phrases.english: If he had one type in large quantity
and one type in small quantity —
he does not say to sell from the plentiful
and to buy from the scarce,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נוֹתְנִין לוֹ שְׁנֵי מִינִין מִן הַמְרוּבֶּה
phrases.english: rather, they give him two of the plentiful type
phrases.notes: Literally "two kinds," but it means two tools of that one kind.

phrases.english: and whatever he has of the scarce type.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה לוֹ מִין אֶחָד מְרוּבֶּה וּמִין אֶחָד מוּעָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two-of-each rule to a case of uneven tools
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no selling and buying to balance the tools. He keeps two of the plentiful type and all he has of the scarce type.

steps.title: One who gives all his property to הקדש loses even his תפילין
steps.stepSummary: In contrast to the person who owes ערכין, someone who declares all his property הקדש loses everything, even his תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who declares all his property הקדש: they take his תפילין too.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the person who owes ערכין with someone who gave all his property to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who owes ערכין keeps his תפילין and other basic items. Someone who said "all my property is הקדש" gave away everything with his own words, so even his תפילין are included.

keyTerms.meaning: One who declares all his property הקדש
Literally "bring up": they count it toward הקדש
The black boxes with פסוקים worn during weekday prayer

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the allowances belong only to someone collected from for a debt of ערכין. They do not apply when a person gives his own property away.

phrases.english: One who consecrates his property —
they take up his phylacteries (תפילין) too.
phrases.notes: He means his תפילין are counted as part of what goes to הקדש. They are not left for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 19, where the person who owes ערכין keeps his תפילין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who declares all his property הקדש does not keep even his תפילין.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source of these allowances
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the treasurer leaves these items. It starts to answer with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the reason behind the משנה's list. It is setting up a פסוק that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is why someone who owes ערכין is not stripped of everything. The words דאמר קרא show that the answer will come from a פסוק, which is quoted right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Because the פסוק says

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason?
Because the verse states:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for leaving the person who owes ערכין these items
